issues.description: The type of the price field for StockIngredient is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement's UML specifies price as int (StockIngredient(String, int, int)), the solution uses an int price field and int getPrice(), but the provided template defines the price field and getter as double. This mismatch can confuse students about whether to use int or double for ingredient prices and leads to inconsistent method/field types when they implement SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery which are specified to use int price.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the price type across all artifacts. Preferably change the template's StockIngredient.price and getPrice() to use int (matching the UML/problem statement and the solution), so students implement calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery with int prices without type confusion. Alternatively, if double prices are intended, update the problem statement and solution to use double consistently.

issues.description: The constructor parameter type for StockIngredient differs between artifacts: the problem statement (UML) and solution expect StockIngredient(String, int, int) while the template provides StockIngredient(String, double, int). This difference can confuse students when they create new StockIngredient instances (e.g., in acceptSupplyDelivery) and when deciding the signature to use in their implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter types consistent. Update the template StockIngredient constructor to accept an int for price (StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity)) to match the problem UML and the solution. Alternatively, adjust the problem statement and solution to accept double if that is the intended design.
